name: fclones-scheduler
description: Find and deduplicate files on a schedule, reclaiming wasted disk space automatically. Runs the fclones duplicate finder against a share on an interval and reports duplicates found and space reclaimable in the container log. The default action only reports. Switch the action to link (replace duplicates with hardlinks), remove (delete duplicates) or dedupe (reflink) once a report has shown you what it would touch. No web UI, no open port.

paths.name: Scan path
paths.description: The share or folder to scan for duplicates, e.g. /mnt/user/Media (read-write is needed for link, remove and dedupe)

paths.name: Cache
paths.description: fclones hash cache and the last-scan record; keeps rescans fast and the schedule stable across restarts

variables.name: Action
variables.description: What to do with duplicates: group (report only), link (hardlink), remove (delete), dedupe (reflink). Anything but group modifies your files

variables.name: Scan interval
variables.description: Time between scans as a Go duration (3h, 12h, 24h). off = no schedule, trigger scans by hand; 0 = run one scan and exit

variables.name: Scan paths
variables.description: Container paths to scan, space-separated; each needs its own path mapping. Leave at /scandir unless you add more mappings

variables.name: Scan arguments
variables.description: Extra flags for the fclones group (scan) phase, e.g. --name '*.mkv' --name '*.mp4' or --rf-over 1; flags and their values only

variables.name: Action arguments
variables.description: Extra flags for the action phase, e.g. --priority bottom; --dry-run previews the action without changing files

variables.name: Scan timeout
variables.description: Per-phase timeout as a Go duration; raise it when a first scan of a large share exceeds 12h, 0 disables it

variables.name: Log level
variables.description: Minimum log level: debug, info, warn or error

variables.name: Allow unsafe arguments
variables.description: Set to true to allow the --transform, --in-place and --no-copy fclones flags, which are refused by default
